newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen sees US$550 mln in '97 acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Loewen sees US$550 mln in '97 acquisitions.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc said on Monday that it expects to complete US$550 million to US$600 million in acquisitions this year.
The funeral home operator said it agreed or closed US$569 million in deals through the end of the second quarter. In total it said those acquisitions would add US$258 million in annualized revenues.
Loewen in May said it stood by an earlier forecast that acquisitions would total US$600 million for the year and said that appeared to be a conservative estimate.
Chief executive officer Ray Loewen made the latest prediction in a conference call with analysts on Tuesday.
Chief financial officer Paul Wagler told the call that the return on investment on those deals was projected to exceed 16 percent for the year.
Wagler said in a later interview that acquisition levels were subject to great volatility and no trend should be inferred from the latest projection.

Loewen earlier announced earnings for the second quarter of US$0.38 a share or US$23.9 million, up from US$0.30 a share or US$17.4 million. According to an average of analysts' estimates compiled by First Call, Loewen had been expected to earn US$0.37 a share.
The second-quarter results were boosted by a pre-tax gain of US$3 million from the sale of 18 Wisconsin funeral homes, which Loewen officials said was equivalent to about US$1.9 million after taxes.
Wagler said the gain was used to reduce general and administrative expenses.

Loewen's portfolio of properties has grown so large that minor divestitures are now routine as the company rationalizes operations within certain geographic areas, vice president of finance Dwight Hawes said.
As a result, such gains are now considered "routine and a matter of course" and part of operating earnings, Wagler said.
Analysts said the gain boosted earnings per share by more than US$0.03 a share and one analyst disagreed that this should be considered part of operating earnings.
Commenting on an industrywide trend, Loewen officials said there was an unexpected decline in the death rate in the second quarter of 4.9 percent in the biggest U.S. cities.
Wagler said that syndication was "going very well" on its previously announced plan to increase its U.S. credit facility to US$1 billion from US$750 million.
Moreover, Loewen's current capital structure is believed to be "sufficient" to fund its growth to mid-1998, he said.
Commenting on consensus earnings estimates of US$1.57 a share for the year, Wagler said Loewen believes "that is the most realistic number we are aware of at this point in time."

Loewen also announced the closure of a regional office in Cincinnati, Ohio. It said costs associated with the closure would not be great. Direct savings will likely total more than US$500,000 this year and US$1.5 million to US$2 million a year in the future. Total savings should be greater when travel and communications efficiencies are included, the company said.
Loewen said it expected to meet its goal for the year of reducing general and administrative expenses to below eight percent of revenues.
Loewen earlier announced the sale of its stake in Arbor Memorial Services Inc to rival Service Corp International for US$69 million. Arbor has long been viewed as a potential takeover target.
Wagler said Loewen felt it could employ its capital better elsewhere. While it continues to have a "long term interest" in Arbor, Loewen "respects Arbor's desire to remain independent," he said.
-- Cynthia Osterman ((Reuters Vancouver Bureau (604) 664-7314))
